references.text: Jesus' self-sacrifice as the good shepherd who lays down his life for the sheep, paralleling his own declaration that he lays down his life voluntarily.
The immediate context in which the Father loves the Son because He lays down His life and has received commandment to take it up again.
The Passover procession where Pilatus claims to have power over life and death, while Jesus confirms that all authority has been given to Him by the Father.
The Father has given the Son to have life in Himself and has granted Him authority to judge, reflecting the authority to give and take life.
The Father's will is that the Son should not lose anything of what He has received, but raise it up on the last day, which connects to Jesus' ability to take His life up again.
